notes: The scheduler no longer plans work for after a task is due. It never checked the due date at all — it walked the week looking for any free gap — so a task due Tuesday could be given a Saturday slot and the run would still report success. Now nothing is placed past its deadline, and anything already overdue keeps getting the earliest slot going.

Deadlines now decide the order, with priority breaking ties between things due the same day. Priority used to come first, which is how a critical task due in three weeks took the slots in front of an ordinary one due tomorrow.

When a task genuinely cannot fit before its deadline, it books what it can and tells you what is left over, instead of scheduling nothing at all. Two of three hours planned beats an empty calendar, and you find out you are short while there is still time to move something.
